quest.title: Past and Future
quest.description: Mavuika's spirit enters the Night Kingdom at a critical moment to extract everyone. She seems to still be at the Speaker's Chamber. Time to go visit her.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x925, Primogem x30, Mora x40575, The Cornerstone of Stars and Flames x1, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.title: Black Stone Under a White Stone

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, there's a lot less stuff here than before...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It's good to see you all here in one piece.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I know you must have a lot of questions, but let Chuychu check you over first. It's best not to let any lingering effects of the Abyss go untreated.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Thank goodness you made it back! I came here as soon as the Pyro Archon told me about your plan.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Take a seat, everybody. I'll examine you one by one...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Despite the short stint in the Night Kingdom, Mualani and the others all have some degree of Abyssal contamination.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: But, thanks to Chuychu's extensive experience treating Abyssal contamination, the harmful effects will not be permanent.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The treatment also relieves Kachina's symptoms.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Alright, that should do it for now. But just to be safe, I'll perform another check-up in a couple of days.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: I have to say, though... I've never seen anyone react to the Abyss like you, Traveler. It's like you're completely immune to its power.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{M#He}{F#She}'s always been special like that. {M#He}{F#She} can even purify its power. Wait, now that you mention it, Paimon doesn't think she's affected, either...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We don't know why, though.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Given the current situation, that ability will likely play a great role in the events to come.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Of course! I still have patients to see, so I'll head out.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Thank you, Chuychu.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Alright, alright... We might not see eye to eye, but we both had good intentions.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Just give it time. I'm sure we'll figure things out between us one day.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Yeah...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Alright... There's so much to discuss, I don't even know where to begin. You've seen it for yourselves, now... the devastation in the Night Kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: ...I'll get straight to the point. Natlan is on the verge of destruction. It's very possible our nation has less than a year before total devastation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: N—N—No... Th—That can't be true, can it!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Less than a year...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's right, but I've only ever disclosed that fact to the handful of people working with me to save this nation.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Our looming destruction is not a recent development, but the inevitable conclusion of the disaster the Abyss initiated five hundred years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mualani told us a little bit about that...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Five hundred years ago, all the nations of Teyvat were invaded by the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Unlike the other nations, Natlan never had stable and deep-rooted Ley Lines, so we suffered the worst of the invasion.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The battle against the Abyss was exceedingly long and brutal. In the end, victory came at the cost of our civilization and countless lives.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Even then, it took centuries of solving the disasters caused by the Abyss to finally achieve the peace we know today.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Still, this is but a superficial victory. The forces of the Abyss have merely been driven back underground — their threat to Natlan remains as real as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I—I'd never have guessed...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The problems plaguing the Night Kingdom are all the more complicated because that realm is essentially functioning as Natlan's Ley Lines.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Immediately after the war, our calculations estimated that we would have a maximum of five hundred years before the Night Kingdom was completely lost to the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But at that time, we were a nation of the destitute. Our people no longer believed in victory, nor did they hold hope for the future.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Our civilization was dying, our faith crumbling, and the line of power passed down from the Wayob nearly severed...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: If we didn't bring the nation back together, it would be foolish to even dream of defeating the Abyss in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: So, the Archon had a long and involved discussion with the heroes of each tribe, and finally came up with a five hundred year-long plan to save Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: So that's what happened...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: After finding Kachina, I encountered a strange figure who gave me a series of new memories.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Since the plan was mentioned in those memories... I guess I've been chosen to play an important role in it.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: But, there's still something I don't understand. Those memories showed me the Pyro Archon from back then... and it was you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? But, that doesn't make any sense! The Pyro Archon is supposed to be human. It's impossible for a human to live that long!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's right. The hardest thing for humans to overcome has always been time — or rather, the natural limitations of our lifespan.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: A god can extend a human's life by using a certain amount of divine power, or subjecting them to a curse.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But, as we all know, Natlan doesn't have gods like that. We can only rely on our own methods.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: A human life is like a flame destined to be extinguished. Five hundred years ago, I placed my life within the Sacred Flame.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Only by dying before my time could I have the chance to wake up again.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: So, in other words, this is your... second life?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That was all part of the plan?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Yes. We only managed to defeat the Abyss all those years ago because the tribes came together as one.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: If the Natlan of the future was to have a fighting chance, the Pyro Archons that came after the war had to rebuild the decimated tribes.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The goal was to reunite the people and restore the strength of each tribe's Wayob.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Once a tribe was back to its full strength, the tribe's Wayob would select a "hero," indicating the tribe was once again ready for war.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The chosen would then stand by my side in defense of our nation, just like great heroes of old, five hundred years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: So that means... I'm one of the chosen?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's right. You bear the Ancient Name, "Umoja," the same one held by the hero from your tribe five hundred years ago. It means "unity."

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: After your adventure in the Night Kingdom, I trust you've come to fully understand the meaning of that Name.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, in other words... You always knew who the Wayob were going to pick from each tribe?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Yes. According to the plan, each tribe was supposed to have been fully restored by the time I awoke. But, something went wrong along the way...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The six heroes successfully inherited the Ancient Names from five hundred years ago, but the intel regarding the plan wasn't passed on to them.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Once again, it comes down to the deterioration of the Night Kingdom. Communication between the Sacred Flame and the Wayob has been blocked.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Just like how the Ode of Resurrection failed to bring Kachina back.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Exactly. It's just another tactic the Abyss is using against us. The Abyss may not possess intelligence, but its methods certainly aren't easy to counter.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: If we want to unblock that information from being passed on, my presence alone isn't enough. The Ancient Name bearer must establish a greater connection to their Name.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: So, I've tried my best to help them from the sidelines.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Currently, Xilonen of the Children of Echoes, Kinich of the Scions of the Canopy, and Iansan of the Collective of Plenty have all been acknowledged by their Names.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: During your adventure, you, too, earned the acknowledgement of your Wayob, Mualani. In the process, you gained the memories stored within your Name.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That leaves two people left...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, we have less than a year...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Yes, but we have no choice. We cannot start the plan until all the heroes have been gathered.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's also why I haven't been able to take action despite the urgency of the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: But, if you knew this whole time, why didn't you just tell me about my role in all this? Wouldn't that make everything go a lot faster?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Perhaps, but the opposite could also be true. Knowing your destiny too early could mean failing to realize your full potential.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Just like your determination to save Kachina, I hope your commitment to this endeavor comes from your own strength of will, rather than a sense of obligation.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: So, I suppose you're not going to tell us who the final two heroes are, then...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's right. Their "time" is yet to come. Putting pressure on them beforehand will only hinder their development.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But what if they don't make it in time...?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I can only trust in the judgment of the Wayob.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I have never believed I could solve this crisis alone. In fact, it was precisely because I chose to trust and rely on others that we managed to get this far.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Natlan's salvation lies not in its Archon, or any singular individual, but in us all.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: You're quite perceptive, aren't you? I thought I might get away with avoiding the topic.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Oh, right! All the stuff you stored here before... Where did it go?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Even though I sacrificed my power, I still needed a contingency plan to ensure you would make it back from the Night Kingdom.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: After all, I was the one who allowed you to take that risk, and Mualani has an important role to play in my plan.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: In addition to their sentimental value, the items I stored here held a much more important purpose — "fuel."

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Fuel? Ah, so back then, that's why you...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Yes. The stories embodied by those items are certainly important, but there's an even more significant trait they all share — every item belonged to a hero of Natlan.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Over time, they became imbued with a certain amount of Contending Fire from being carried in battle.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: On their own, each item's power is limited, but, together, their combined effect can prove quite useful in a dire situation.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: By burning those items, I was able to activate the Contending Fire stored within them to open the boundary between the two worlds.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: It was a rather crude approach, so all their power was depleted in an instant, as you can see.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, weren't they all precious treasures? What about their stories...?

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: *sigh* That's exactly why I dragged you all here... No matter what, I never wanted the Pyro Archon to have to use that power.

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: I'm so sorry...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: You have nothing to be sorry for. You all deserve my thanks, actually. If you hadn't saved the totem pole, that area of the Night Kingdom would have been forever lost to the Abyss.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Then, it would only be a matter of time before the Children of Echoes was met with disaster.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Besides, when those heroes entrusted their belongings to me, or the Pyro Archon of their time, it was out of a desire to contribute to Natlan's survival.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: If they knew those items helped save the present-day heroes of Natlan, they would not mourn their loss.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Even when you put it that way, I still feel bad...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Hehe, there's no need. Remember what I told you about "time"?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The people and events of the past are never truly lost to us. We simply carry them with us in a different form. In that sense, we didn't lose anything at all.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: If you still have regrets, let them fuel your resolve in the battles to come.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Your deeds will become new legends and nurture new forms of power, just like the items once stored here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, we'd still like to return the favor...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Haha, if that's the case, just treat me to a drink sometime.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Now that Kachina has returned, we can finally hold the victory feast and celebrate your team's triumph in the Night Warden Wars.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: We could all use the rest, that's for sure. Plus, you'll be able to silence everyone who doubted you once and for all, Kachina.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: *sigh* Still, now that I know the danger we're facing, having a victory feast doesn't feel right...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Try not to let it get to you. It's important to stay calm. Worrying about it will only affect your judgment.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Alright, you should head out. I'll join you in a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: When I was young, I used to sit by the hot springs and listen to the stories of warriors from all over Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: They attract people from all walks of life. Friends come easy here, no matter what tribe you're from.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: The People of the Springs have never claimed the hot springs as their own private property. They are there to bring all "hot spring buddies" together.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: It's been really nice, seeing the children of my tribe get older. It's helped me gradually understand the true value of the springs.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: I've witnessed their energy, their determination, their absolute passion for life...

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: Even when they cause trouble, I never manage to hold on to my anger for long. It's unbelievable how quickly they worm their way back into my good graces.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: I'm certain Mualani will become a great warrior when she grows up. She possesses infinite potential... I can see it.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: One day, when I'm no longer in fighting form, I'll come here and tell stories to all the children, just like those warriors did for me.

dialogues.speaker: Atea
dialogues.text: So, you better get busy, Pyro Archon, or I'll end up running out of stories, hahaha.

dialogues.speaker: Tenoch
dialogues.text: Our nation is engulfed in darkness, our tribes stand divided, and yet you promise victory in the distant future...

dialogues.speaker: Tenoch
dialogues.text: The Abyss is a cunning enemy, one that I've faced in battle many times. Were that not the case, I would never understand exercising this degree of caution.

dialogues.speaker: Tenoch
dialogues.text: My rage will never know absolution, and my power will no longer aid you in victory.

dialogues.speaker: Tenoch
dialogues.text: But, you came to me because you knew you could convince me with just a single sentence.

dialogues.speaker: Tenoch
dialogues.text: I understand your choice. The heroes of today will forge the path ahead with blood and fire. Just remember to earn us the victory we're owed.

dialogues.speaker: Tenoch
dialogues.text: Otherwise, rest assured, I'll find a way to collect the debt.

dialogues.speaker: Tenoch
dialogues.text: ..."For Natlan."

dialogues.speaker: Hine
dialogues.text: So... you're gonna head five hundred years in the future to serve as the Pyro Archon again...

dialogues.speaker: Hine
dialogues.text: But, what about the you from right now? You're just gonna die?

dialogues.speaker: Haumia
dialogues.text: You can't ask her those questions and expect her to answer, my dear. The decision is hers to make, and she deserves our support.

dialogues.speaker: Haumia
dialogues.text: We will do everything we can to rebuild the tribes. Don't you worry.

dialogues.speaker: Haumia
dialogues.text: Even across time, we will all do our part to fight for Natlan's future.

dialogues.speaker: Hine
dialogues.text: Yeah, mom's right! We'll always believe in you, Sis!

dialogues.speaker: Hine
dialogues.text: Seriously, though, Dad should be here. Where is he?

dialogues.speaker: Haumia
dialogues.text: I—I imagine he—he didn't know what to say, so he chose not to come at all. Don't take it to heart, my dear, that's just who he is.

dialogues.speaker: Haumia
dialogues.text: Just remember — no matter what happens in the future, we will always love you.

dialogues.speaker: Hine
dialogues.text: I'll come find you one day!

dialogues.speaker: Hine
dialogues.text: I know I can't live that long, but I'll think of something!

dialogues.speaker: Hine
dialogues.text: There has to be a way for us to meet again one day! If there's an answer out there somewhere, I'm gonna find it!

dialogues.speaker: Hine
dialogues.text: So, don't forget about me!

dialogues.speaker: Ngendi
dialogues.text: If that's your decision, then you have my full support, Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Kalunga
dialogues.text: May our children live to see such a lovely sun.

dialogues.speaker: Fietena
dialogues.text: For Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Nzambe
dialogues.text: No one fights alone.

dialogues.speaker: Voice of the Past
dialogues.text: The rules are my legacy. They shall grant us the strength to overcome the next tragedy.

dialogues.speaker: Voice of the Past
dialogues.text: War forged the six tribes, taught us how to fight, instilled in us what it means to love...

dialogues.speaker: Voice of the Past
dialogues.text: Who will be the one to bring this to an end?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We are the inheritors of memory and legend.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Those who grew alongside sun and wind.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Those who forged our own destiny and future.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That is Natlan's fire, the lifeblood of our nation.

talks.objective: Attend the banquet at the inn

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Chuychu! You here for the victory feast, too?

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Oh, no. I knew Chasca would be here, so I just came to deliver some medicine. I was about to leave, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: It's not that I don't want to celebrate Kachina and the others. I'm so glad she made it back, it's just... I'll make things awkward if I'm around my sister right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, well, you two had a fight, so Paimon can understand...

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: She didn't cause any trouble during your trip, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Of course not.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, she was super helpful! She gave us a lot of useful information about the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: That's good. That's all I needed to know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is there a reason you asked? You were pretty outspoken when we first met, but now it's like you're holding something back...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You can tell us anything.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Maybe it seemed unreasonable, picking that fight with her before you left. But, I did it for a reason.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Her impulse to fight is extremely strong. Her mental strength helps her rein it in, but she still loses control sometimes. I had no idea what you might face in the Night Kingdom, so I didn't want to take any chances...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what you're saying is...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You deliberately provoked her so she'd take that impulse out on you?

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Okay, so maybe it sounds a little... stupid. But, it works pretty well. It helps her keep her cool for a little while, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Anyway, I'm just glad you were able to make it back safe and sound. That's all I wanted.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, do you really have to go that far? Can't you just... talk it out?

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: No way. Chasca never opens up about her own pain, especially to her family. She can't learn about this, or it'll be even harder to help her.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: I appreciate the understanding, and don't worry — I'll find a way to help her ease this burden. Anyway, I need to get going. Enjoy the celebration.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: Oh, and, if you ever need a doctor, you know who to find!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Who would've thought there was a deeper reason behind their arguing...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They're trying to look out for each other in their own way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In the end, it's all the Abyss' fault. Paimon's had enough of them! Hmph!

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Let's give a huge round of applause to our brave young warrior, Kachina!

dialogues.speaker: Teayo
dialogues.text: Woohoo!

dialogues.speaker: Sabea
dialogues.text: Well done, Kachina!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Th—Thank you, everyone! I'm so glad I finally made it.

dialogues.speaker: Weqro
dialogues.text: I always knew you could do it! With so much potential at your age, you have a great future ahead of you!

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: You're one to talk! Don't think I didn't know you were the first person to abandon your team. I'll be dealing with you when we get back.

dialogues.speaker: Weqro
dialogues.text: I—I had no choice! My friend invited me, I couldn't just say no!

dialogues.speaker: Sabea
dialogues.text: Oh really? So you weren't just trying to get ahead in the first round?

dialogues.speaker: Weqro
dialogues.text: I wasn't, I swear! I just happened to find that bearer injured in the wild, so I stopped to bandage his wounds.

dialogues.speaker: Weqro
dialogues.text: When he insisted on repaying the favor, what was I supposed to do? I'm just one person, I figured Kachina would have no trouble replacing me.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: But the fact of the matter is that after your departure, everyone else started thinking about swapping teams too.

dialogues.speaker: Tlaco
dialogues.text: I'm really sorry, Kachina... It was wrong of us to abandon you like that.

dialogues.speaker: Cempoa
dialogues.text: It's amazing that you still made it all the way through to the Night Warden Wars... That's the highest honor.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: So, uh, wh—what about you guys? Did you make it far?

dialogues.speaker: Tlaco
dialogues.text: Umm...

dialogues.speaker: Cempoa
dialogues.text: Our team captain drank too much the night before the competition, and turned up late to the stadium on the day... We got disqualified.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Hahaha, serves you all right! No sympathy from me.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Alright, alright. There's no need to be like that, Uncle Pacal.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Um, dear friends, I'd like to say a few words...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Firstly, I'm grateful to my friends and our Great Archon for helping to bring me back.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: #This Traveler and {M#his}{F#her} companion Paimon are some of the strongest people I've ever met. If they were allowed to participate in the Pilgrimage, I have no doubt that they'd win the whole thing.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: They've agreed to let me learn from them. With their help, I believe I can become even stronger still!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: And let's not forget my good friends, Mualani, Chasca, Kinich, and Iansan... They all helped the Traveler and Paimon figure out a way to bring me back from the Night Kingdom...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: They, too, deserve to be called our heroes. So... please give another round of applause, for them. Thank you so much!

dialogues.speaker: Teayo
dialogues.text: Well said!

dialogues.speaker: Sabea
dialogues.text: I'll drink to that!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hehe, how does it feel being a hero, Kachina?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: To be honest, it's a bit overwhelming... It all just feels so surreal...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, you'd better get used to it! Next stop, undefeated champion!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That way, I'll also become a champion coach.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Hey, please don't make fun of me...

dialogues.speaker: Rezanov
dialogues.text: My lord, we've received word that the Pyro Archon has lost much of her power.

dialogues.speaker: Rezanov
dialogues.text: Although your injury complicates things, this is most certainly the opportune time to seize the Gnosis...

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Victory and defeat are rules, not outcomes. I have never taken advantage of an opponent in a time of weakness, and I don't intend to start now.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: As for you... I must confess, I did not expect that little trick of yours to save the day.
No matter how dense the fog, as long as the sun remains, we cannot turn day into night. She could have dispelled it — she simply chose not to.
You don't have much time, and you're injured on top of that. What do you plan to do next?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: I'm beginning to see just how useful you may turn out to be.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: You... heard something from here, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here. Have some fruit juice — I got it specially for you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How did you know? That's Paimon's favorite!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: You look like you've still got questions. Ask away.

choices.text: Isn't your plan a little convoluted?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Because they had their own lives to live.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The thought of telling them, abandon your families and everyone you love, and come with me to the end of time, for in five hundred years, Natlan will be destroyed... It seemed too cruel.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: You could just as easily point out that everything in this world will come to an end eventually. But life is short, and beyond a point it just doesn't seem real.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Imagine if I said, "Let's leave right now and go save the sun, because it'll flame out in a few million years"... It would sound quite ridiculous.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I couldn't make them shoulder that burden with me.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Besides, every generation will have its heroes, this one included. The plan could still work without them.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Or of course, without me. But since I was the one who came up with the plan, I felt duty-bound to see it through to the end.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's suddenly remembering that portrait in your room. Was that... your family from back then?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Yes, it was. So when you asked me who my sister grew up to be, the truth is that very little information survives.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: From what I've been able to piece together, I can conclude with a reasonable degree of confidence that she ended up as an architect and artist.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: She played an instrumental role in rebuilding the Scions of the Canopy tribe, designing and building many houses. But of course, none of her buildings are around anymore.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Still, it was an impressive achievement, and I'm very proud of her.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So that's the life you had to leave behind...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: You feel loss keenly. It seems to stir up feelings of regret in you... But this is something I have long since come to terms with.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: This is a war, and there can be no war without loss. I am already far more fortunate than those who lost their lives to the Abyss.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The people of Natlan look to me as their Archon, and the weight of their expectations is mine to bear. I must see our fate through to the very end, no matter what I may find there.

choices.text: That's actually what I wanted to ask...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, doesn't that mean the way everything ends has already been written, including your plan?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I suppose, but so what? Don't forget, time takes many forms. The past, present, and future co-exist, and all are equally important.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Even if the future ends in destruction, that's still no reason to give up on the here and now.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: And it's precisely because we humans cannot know our fate that we will never give up on our struggle.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: This is a pivotal moment. We are still two heroes short.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Well... three, to be precise. There's one further hero who I'm hoping to get on my side, whatever it takes.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Surely you don't mean me?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Your resistance to the corrupting power of the Abyss is truly remarkable. It would easily make you an all-important figure in the upcoming battle.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: If you agree to join us, you will not only gain my full support in your journey, but I will also forge a brand new Ancient Name for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ancient Names... can be forged?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: They can. Several strict conditions must be met, but if they couldn't be forged at all, then the number of them in circulation would have long dwindled to zero.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Possessing an ancient name would mean that your adventures in Natlan are recorded in full. Your stories would be remembered by our people for all the years to come.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The Ode of Resurrection may have temporarily lost its power, but still... Take this as my personal guarantee that I shall never let you fall.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Just like in the Night Kingdom, I will be there for you. That is a promise I will fulfill at all costs. This nation always honors its heroes.

choices.text: You don't have to promise me anything.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we can't just ignore the situation here.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Wonderful. Then I'll reach out to Xilonen right away. She's the one who will forge the Name.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: We've never forged an Ancient Name for an outlander before, but I trust she'll find a way.

choices.text: I just want to help out the people.
Why didn't you get the heroes of the past to join you in this age?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I've been through so much all at once. Everything still kinda feels like a dream.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you still feeling unwell?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Nope, all better now! Hehe, I told you I bounce back pretty quick. So don't worry about me.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I bet you guys must be tired, though. Make sure you get some good rest tonight. You gotta recharge so you'll be in the mood to have fun!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: At previous victory feasts, you'd always find me in the crowd, singing and dancing. But after what I found out today... It's too much. I'm still trying to process it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It does feel weird, seeing you so out of sorts...

choices.text: Natlan's fall isn't set in stone though, right?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Is this another pearl of wisdom based on your adventuring experience?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well, Paimon agrees with {NICKNAME}! Everyone's come together to celebrate Kachina's achievements. That's gotta be a first.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: You're right. Hehe, Kachina looks really happy. And now I'm being the moody one...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Ugh, enough doom and gloom. Time to shake it off!

choices.text: It's important to try and enjoy moments like this when they come along.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Alright, Kachina! Let's party!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I—I'm a little embarrassed...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Don't be! Come on, you're the star of the show today!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: My apologies. I knew more than I let on.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Everything comes at a price, and most heroes aren't people who set out to become a hero.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: If you cling too tightly to your goal, you end up losing things that are far more precious.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: But in any case, we're now on the same page.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I wonder how long before the two final heroes appear, from the Flower-Feather Clan and the Masters of the Night-Wind...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It's rare to meet travelers as strong and brave as yourselves. I raise my glass to you.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Anyway, my sister's already gone back to our tribe. She has patients to treat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we actually ran into her on our way here, and uhh... Well, Paimon just thinks she really cares about you!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Yeah... I'm planning on visiting home myself in a few days, to tell her and the rest of the family that they need to be extra careful. I just hope they'll take it seriously.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: The Abyss has likely sensed your arrival in Natlan by now. So exercise caution on your adventures as well.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: It cost us a lot, but we got Kachina back safely, and that's what matters.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: There'll be even tougher challenges coming our way in the days ahead, though. We'll have to train harder, make sure we're in peak condition.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: That includes you, Paimon. I can do a special one-off session to show you the ropes, interested?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, n—no thanks...
